questions.boundary: The boundary of the Catalog Management bounded context (catalog-management) becomes a broker boundary. Its two services produce and consume on Apache Kafka (kafka:29092). Every other service stays on Redpanda (redpanda:29092). Event bindings that cross the context boundary now also cross the Kafka/Redpanda boundary, and MirrorMaker 2 bridges them in one direction per topic.

Catalog-service on Kafka must keep receiving TenantUpdated and TenantDeleted from tenant-service, which stays on Redpanda, through the redpanda->kafka flow. Its consumer position must carry over (committed offset 1, set explicitly in P09). Skipping an event misses a tenant DB migration or cleanup; replaying one re-runs migrations or cleanup.
candidates.ecommerce-category-query-service|catalog: Attribute updates must keep reaching the category read model on Redpanda through the kafka->redpanda flow. The binding is undeclared (PROMISE_COVERAGE_MISSING), so a plan built only from declared bindings would leave it out.
CategoryUpdated events must keep reaching the category read model on Redpanda through the kafka->redpanda flow, under the same topic name and in order.
candidates.ecommerce-image-service|tenant.tenant.ev: The same as for catalog-service: image-service must keep receiving tenant lifecycle events through the redpanda->kafka flow, and keep its offset (1). This drives tenant migrations and the S3 tenant cleaner, which wipes the tenant's image prefix when a tenant is deleted.
Attribute updates must still reach the product read model on Redpanda through the kafka->redpanda flow under the unchanged topic name. AIP has no catalog promise for this binding, so only the observed attachment shows it exists.

The product read model must keep receiving ProductUpdated/ProductDeleted from catalog-service and ProductImagePromoted from image-service, both now produced on Kafka. The kafka->redpanda flow must deliver them under the same topic name, per product_id key in order, with headers intact. Otherwise storefront product data and image URLs go stale.
